cover_tag: AI-curated research brief for discussion with a clinical team
bottom_line: Ketamine remains a research hypothesis for WWOX-related epilepsy. The reviewed sources do not establish benefit in WWOX-DEE, either for an acute episode or for ongoing seizure control.

rows.statement: Spontaneous bursts occurred in 36 of 42 neuronal Wwox-knockout slices, 4 of 23 heterozygous slices and 0 of 11 wild-type slices (cortical slices, postnatal days 13 to 17; slices are nested within animals).
rows.model: Mouse cortical slice; spontaneous burst occurrence. Animal denominators: PLACEHOLDER

rows.statement: d-APV, a competitive NMDA receptor antagonist, abolished bursts in five knockout slices from three knockout animals. Ketamine and memantine were not tested.
rows.model: Mouse cortical slice, neuronal Wwox loss; burst abolition. 5 slices, 3 animals

rows.statement: Carbenoxolone was reported to lower burst frequency by 87% without reversal after washout. It is nonselective, and a pannexin blocker failed to reproduce the effect. The paper's duration and amplitude descriptions differ from its figure.
After d-APV washout the frequency bar was about 1.8 times baseline by image reading. The error bar includes baseline and the text describes recovery, so rebound is unproven.
rows.model: Same slice model; burst frequency after washout (image reading)

rows.statement: The result supports a contribution of NMDA receptor signalling to bursts in that preparation. A change in inhibition, network drive or intrinsic excitability could still set the bursts off, and the pharmacological evidence traces to one laboratory and one preparation.
rows.model: Inference from W1 to W4; not a separate measurement

rows.statement: The separate Wwox studies that used ketamine for anaesthesia supplied no controlled seizure endpoint for ketamine.

groups.title: B. Clinical data from other indications (not WWOX)

rows.statement: Ket-Mid randomised 144 children. Clinical cessation at five minutes was 76% with ketamine plus midazolam and 21% with placebo plus midazolam: a first-line add-on result in mixed causes.
rows.model: Initial convulsive status epilepticus, children; cessation at 5 min

rows.statement: KETASER01 stopped at 10 participants; 2 of 5 in each arm met the study endpoint. There are too few randomised data for comparative efficacy.
rows.model: Refractory convulsive status epilepticus, children; study endpoint

rows.statement: In a three-infant series, seizure resolution and changes in co-infusions were not aligned in a way that isolates ketamine.

A memantine trial in mixed developmental and epileptic encephalopathy lists 9 of 27 versus 2 of 27 on a composite crossover outcome. The paired overlap is unavailable to the laboratory; paired significance and harms are unresolved.
The original 24 of 30 pooled claim and the proposed genetically favourable subgroup failed review. An ATP1A2 case supplied concurrent add-on treatment, not a validated ketamine-to-memantine sequence.

groups.title: C. The proposed comparison (not yet performed)

rows.statement: Transfer from d-APV to ketamine requires two comparisons: receptor action under active conditions, and the exposure at which each effect was measured. Total plasma, free plasma, CSF, brain and bath concentrations were not related to one another in the relevant setting.

Ketamine reduced the hyperpolarisation-activated current Ih in cortical pyramidal neurons at a nearby developmental age, and the effect disappeared in HCN1-knockout neurons. This is a plausible rival if sag and burst frequency change together; Wwox-dependent sensitivity is unknown.
rows.model: Cortical pyramidal neurons, other preparation; Ih

rows.statement: S-ketamine suppressed induced events in adult hippocampal slices without magnesium. The reported bath observation started at 100 µM, about 11 times the highest total human plasma peak in the sources, around 8.9 µM.
rows.model: Adult hippocampal slice, no Mg2+; nominal bath concentration vs total plasma (not unbound)

rows.statement: A pore blocker may suppress Wwox-related bursts when its effect on NMDA receptor activity is comparable to that of d-APV.
rows.model: Not tested; needs the P5 design

rows.statement: Compare ketamine, memantine and d-APV with vehicle in the same slice model. Record burst rate, evoked inhibition, Ih sag, and early and later washout, with the probe schedule. Supports the class hypothesis if both pore blockers suppress bursts at comparable evoked block; weakens it if both fail at verified depth while d-APV reproduces its effect. One failed agent weakens only that agent.
rows.model: Mouse cortical slice, neuronal Wwox loss. Thresholds and replication numbers: PLACEHOLDER

n1: d-APV abolished spontaneous bursts in 5 Wwox-knockout slices from 3 animals (bursts in 36 of 42 knockout slices).
n2: NMDA receptor activation contributes to the bursts, in this preparation only.
n3a: d-APV abolishes bursts. Tested in the Wwox slice.
n3b: Ketamine or memantine suppress bursts at matched evoked NMDA block. Not tested in Wwox tissue.
n4: Ih (HCN1) sag change or interneuron disinhibition produces the ketamine effect instead.
n5: Same slice: ketamine, memantine, d-APV, vehicle. Burst rate, evoked inhibition, Ih sag, washout.

corpus: Peer-reviewed sources named in the reference list and LEGEND's own audits of them. Search strategy, inclusion rules and the number of records screened: PLACEHOLDER

The audit found all 25 cited PMIDs and matched 23 of 24 quotations. Those checks were kept separate from judging what each citation supports. Figures were re-read and the pharmacokinetic arithmetic was reproduced.

Full-text routes remained blocked for key memantine, Kuki and Rosati papers. Ket-Mid was read as a published abstract. Underlying patient records, treatment plans and individual timings are not included.

The 24 of 30 pooled claim and genetic subgroup failed review. The claim of a unique mechanism match was overstated. Only two of nine initial labels of the GSK3 duration-switch comparison matched the paper in one audit, and the apparent short-versus-long reversal did not survive.
Exploratory. No validated predictive probability is given and none should be read from this brief.
methods.figure2_reserved: Figure 2 (quantitative comparison) is not drawn. A figure is added only when the content pack states, for every plotted value, the assay, the unit, the exposure definition (nominal solution, total or unbound), the setting (clinical or animal) and, where the source gives them, an interval. Mixed settings are never pooled and no dose is shown.
